definition: The stretch of a record where the band drops out and the drums play alone; the part DJs looped.
The four-bar drum solo from The Winstons' "Amen, Brother" (1969), played by G.C. Coleman.
The drum loop from Lyn Collins's "Think (About It)" (1972), played by Jabo Starks.
A short shouted or sung fragment used as a hit, like the two-word shout from "Think (About It)".
DJ Kool Herc's routine of cutting between breaks on two turntables.
A 25-LP series on Street Beat Records that put the best-known breaks on cheap compilations.
Cutting a break into single hits and putting them back in a new order, as jungle did to the Amen break.
A sound chosen for scratching, such as the "fresh" line from "Change the Beat".
A new performance recorded to stand in for a sample, as with the Kraftwerk parts on "Planet Rock".
Re-performing part of an existing song instead of lifting the recording.
In Jamaican music, an instrumental backing that many vocalists record over.
The 1985 riddim built on the "rock" preset of the Casio MT-40.
A factory rhythm or sound built into an instrument.
The TR-808 beat from DJ Battery Brain's 1988 single that underpinned 1990s funk carioca.
The drum pattern that replaced the Volt Mix in 2000s funk carioca.
Soul vocals sampled and pitched up, the early-2000s sound tied to Kanye West and Just Blaze.
Music recorded for licensing to film, TV and radio, with the library usually owning the whole copyright.
